title.narrative: Response for HIV and for STIs in Madagascar; an approach involving the populations most exposed in the zones of vulnerability - Madagascar (01-Oct-2011-30-Jun-2016)

description.narrative: Uniquely among southern African countries, Madagascar has a low prevalence of HIV. The program supported by this grant aims to maintain the prevalence of HIV to less than one percent among the general population and to improve the quality of life of people living with HIV. The program will focus on key populations most at risk of HIV infection in 152 vulnerable communities in eight regions. Grant funds will be used to provide antiretroviral treatment and prevention and treatment of opportunistic infections; to provide prevention services including counseling, testing and treatment for sexually transmitted infections, HIV counseling and testing, family planning, prevention of mother-to-child transmission and condom distribution services; to organize communication campaigns addressing stigma and discrimination; and to organize targeted advocacy and information campaigns. The program targets commercial sex workers and their clients; men who have sex with men; prisoners; injecting drug users; marginalized youth; people living with HIV; and pregnant women.
